the hybrid wheel loader conﬁrmed that the presented control

The proposed approach relies on correct state detection
to trigger optimization based on predicted power demand.
In practical implementation, when state detection conﬁdence
is insufﬁcient or misclassiﬁcation is detected, the controller
intentionally disables the DP–PMP optimization and falls
back to a conservative baseline strategy, such as a rule-
based controller or adaptive ECMS. This fallback mechanism
ensures robust and safe operation under uncertain or unfore-
seen conditions, while preserving the beneﬁts of optimization
when reliable predictions are available.
Future research could focus on analyzing the potential
for reducing raw pollutant emissions through reduced tran-
sient ICE operation, thanks to hybridization. Furthermore, the
integration of emission control into the optimization control
framework to investigate the optimal concept for exhaust
aftertreatment systems is another area for future studies.
In addition, the provision of future scenarios through the
networking of machines and their management as a ﬂeet on
the construction site is another research focus.
